S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.

subtypes.Intrusive Memories: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Distressing Dreams: Recurrent distressing dreams in which the content and/or affect of the dream are related to the traumatic event.
subtypes.Dissociative Reactions (Flashbacks): Dissociative reactions (e.g., flashbacks) in which the individual feels or acts as if the traumatic event were recurring.
subtypes.Psychological Distress at Cues: Intense or prolonged psychological distress at exposure to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Physiological Reactions to Cues: Marked physiological reactions to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.

subtypes.Internal Avoidance: Efforts to avoid distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings about or closely associated with the traumatic event.
subtypes.External Avoidance: Efforts to avoid external reminders (people, places, conversations, activities, objects, situations) that arouse distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings.

S072.name: Negative_Beliefs
S072.description: Persistent and exaggerated negative beliefs or expectations about oneself, others, or the world.

subtypes.Negative Self-Beliefs: Distorted beliefs such as 'I am fundamentally bad,' 'I am damaged,' or 'I am worthless'.
subtypes.Negative Beliefs about Others: Distorted beliefs such as 'No one can be trusted' or 'Others are dangerous'.
subtypes.Negative Worldview: Extreme beliefs such as 'The world is completely dangerous' or 'Life is meaningless'.

S074.name: Persistent_Negative_Emotional_State
S074.description: Persistent negative emotional state (e.g., fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame).

subtypes.Persistent Fear: A state of constant fear, anxiety, and tension.
subtypes.Persistent Horror: The shock and terror of the traumatic moment do not fade and remain.
subtypes.Persistent Anger: A state of chronic anger boiling inside or being expressed aggressively.
subtypes.Persistent Guilt: Unceasing feelings of guilt or remorse related to the trauma.
subtypes.Persistent Shame: Continuing to feel shame or humiliation due to the trauma.

S077.name: Irritability_Aggression
S077.description: Irritable behavior and angry outbursts (with little or no provocation) typically expressed as verbal or physical aggression.

subtypes.Impulsive Anger: Sudden explosions of anger for trivial reasons or no clear reason.
subtypes.Verbal Aggression: Attacking others with shouting, cursing, or blame without holding back.
subtypes.Physical Aggression: Physically attacking people or throwing/breaking objects.
subtypes.Chronic Irritability: A state where nerves are always sharp and sensitive, ready to explode at the slightest touch.

S078.name: Reckless_Self_Destructive_Behavior
S078.description: Reckless or self-destructive behavior pattern that endangers one's safety or health.

subtypes.Risky Behaviors: Reckless actions disregarding consequences, such as speeding, dangerous sports, or criminal acts.
subtypes.Substance Abuse: Excessive drinking or drug use to harm oneself.
subtypes.Indisicriminate Sexual Behavior: Engaging in unprotected or dangerous sexual activities repetitively.
subtypes.Self-Harm: Actions that intentionally harm or scar one's own body.

patient_info.stressor: Sigfredo was seriously injured during an early-morning solo hike along a wet Salish Sea bluff trail, where a partial trail collapse left him trapped until another hiker found him. In the weeks after returning home, he tried to keep working at the telecom call center and studying for his GED, but over four months the accident became tied to worsening sleep, intrusive recollections, avoidance of coastal trails and even hiking friends, persistent fear and shame about being “careless,” sharper anger on customer calls, and unsafe late-night driving to prove he was fine. His performance dropped enough that missed CRM entries and a heated call escalation threatened his team-lead prospects. He eventually used his employer’s assistance program after a supervisor framed it as a way to protect both his job and his plans for school.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: I came in because I barely sleep right anymore—I'll lie there hearing rain or thinking about the bluff giving way, then when I do pass out I wake up sweaty from dreams and show up to the call center feeling like I never slept.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
S069.manifestation: Stuff pops in my head out of nowhere, like the sound of rocks sliding or my leg stuck under me, and for a minute I'm back on that trail instead of sitting at my desk with a headset on.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.
S070.manifestation: I won't go near the coast trails now, and I dodge texts from my hiking buddies because even talking about going out there makes my chest tighten.

S072.name: Negative_Beliefs
S072.description: Persistent and exaggerated negative beliefs or expectations about oneself, others, or the world.
S072.manifestation: I keep thinking I was stupid and careless for being out there alone, and now it feels like if I let my guard down anywhere something bad is going to happen.

S074.name: Persistent_Negative_Emotional_State
S074.description: Persistent negative emotional state (e.g., fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame).
S074.manifestation: Most days I feel scared and embarrassed under the surface, like everyone can tell I messed up and I'm not as tough as I used to act.

S077.name: Irritability_Aggression
S077.description: Irritable behavior and angry outbursts (with little or no provocation) typically expressed as verbal or physical aggression.
S077.manifestation: At work my patience is way shorter, and I've snapped at customers over small stuff and even raised my voice enough that my supervisor had to pull me aside.

S078.name: Reckless_Self_Destructive_Behavior
S078.description: Reckless or self-destructive behavior pattern that endangers one's safety or health.
S078.manifestation: Some nights I get in my car and drive too fast on dark, wet roads just to prove to myself I'm not afraid, even though I know it's dumb and could get me hurt again.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: My work has slipped enough that I missed important CRM notes and got written up after a call escalation, and now I’m worried I blew my chance at moving toward team lead. I’ve also fallen behind on GED studying because I’m exhausted and avoiding people I used to hike with.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on for about four months, ever since I got trapped after the bluff trail collapsed.
